Title: Effects of transdermal testosterone application on the ovarian response to FSH in poor responders undergoing assisted reproduction technique—a prospective, randomized, double-blind study
Author: N. Massin et al.
Comment: The paper analysed 25 placebo and 24 testosterone participants per protocol, whereas the synthesis contract requires women randomized as denominators. Accordingly, the explicitly reported randomized totals (26 and 27) are used with the treated-cycle delivery counts (1 and 2). The paper did not report an odds ratio, confidence interval, or treatment-versus-placebo significance test for delivery. One testosterone-allocated participant discontinued because of spontaneous pregnancy; no delivery outcome for that pregnancy was reported, so it was not counted as a live birth.
Study Environment: Reproductive Medicine Unit, Jean Verdier Hospital
Topic of Content: Testosterone pretreatment before ovarian stimulation in poor responders undergoing IVF or ICSI
Participant type: Women with previous poor ovarian response and decreased ovarian reserve undergoing IVF or ICSI
Recruitment source: Reproductive Medicine Unit, Jean Verdier Hospital
Outcome measurement: Number of deliveries per woman randomized

Title: Transdermal testosterone pretreatment in poor responders undergoing ICSI: a randomized clinical trial
Author: Bosdou et al.
Comment: The paper reports a rate difference rather than an odds ratio. No odds ratio was calculated or inserted; the directly reported ITT event counts (2/26 versus 2/24) should be used by the synthesis to calculate its planned odds ratio. The negative signs in the supplied OCR are corrupted in some prose, but Table IV and the group rates identify the reported difference as -0.6 percentage points with 95% CI -19.0 to +16.9.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Transdermal testosterone pretreatment, 10 mg/day for 21 days') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)

Content length: 10 mg/day for 21 days before ovarian stimulation
Topic of Content: Testosterone pretreatment before ovarian stimulation in poor ovarian responders undergoing ICSI
Participant type: Women meeting Bologna criteria for poor ovarian response and undergoing ICSI
Recruitment source: Unit for Human Reproduction, Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, in cooperation with the Unit for Human Reproduction, University of Thessaly

Title: The Efect of Transdermal Testosterone Gel Pretreatment on IVF Outcomes in Patients with Poor Ovarian Reserve
Author: Nidhi Sharma; Kanad D Nayar
Comment: Live birth was not reported, so ongoing pregnancy was extracted. The Results narrative conflicts with Table 3, stating 27.5% vs 22.9% (p = 0.45), whereas Table 3 reports explicit counts of 15/46 vs 10/41 (p = 0.39); Table 3 was used. The paper also contains inconsistent allocation descriptions: the abstract/Methods state 41 treatment and 46 control, while the Results tables identify TTG n=46 and control n=41. No odds ratio was reported by the paper, so the odds-ratio fields were left null; raw event counts were retained for synthesis.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('TTG group (transdermal testosterone gel 12.5 mg/day)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
domain: Assisted reproduction / IVF in women with diminished ovarian reserve
Content length: Pretreatment from day 6 of the previous menstrual cycle through day 2 of the stimulated cycle
Participant type: Women with diminished ovarian reserve undergoing IVF
Outcome measurement: Ongoing pregnancy rate per cycle initiated; patients were followed to 12 weeks of pregnancy

Title: Role of transdermal testosterone gel pre-treatment on IVF outcome: a prospective randomized controlled trial with active control
Author: Singh N, Parimalam P, Kumar S, Vanamail P
Comment: The RESULTS text states that 34 testosterone participants and 35 controls were analyzed for pregnancy outcomes because one testosterone participant did not undergo embryo transfer, but Table 2 presents live-birth events/rates under N=35 for each randomized group. Per the synthesis contract, intention-to-treat randomized denominators (35 vs 35) were retained. The reported percentages appear to use 34 as the testosterone denominator (5/34=14.7%), whereas the extracted ITT count is 5/35. No odds ratio was reported by the paper, so it was not entered.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Transdermal testosterone gel pretreatment plus standard IVF/ICSI treatment') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Prospective randomized controlled trial with active control
Study Environment: Assisted Reproductive Technology Centre, AIIMS, New Delhi
Topic of Content: Transdermal testosterone gel pretreatment before IVF/ICSI in women with previous poor ovarian response
Participant type: Women aged 39 years or younger with a previously failed IVF/ICSI cycle and 5 or fewer oocytes retrieved in the previous cycle, with normal ovarian reserve and normal or low testosterone levels
Recruitment source: Assisted Reproductive Technology Centre, Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, AIIMS, New Delhi
Outcome measurement: Any birth after 24 weeks gestation resulting in delivery of a live infant, calculated per cycle

Title: Therapeutic effect of prolonged testosterone pretreatment in women with poor ovarian response: A randomized control trial
Author: Hoang et al.
Comment: The adjusted OR is from multivariable logistic regression. Although the paper says analyses were intention-to-treat and reports final/randomized group n=42, Table 3 calculates this outcome among n=40 control and n=40 in the 4-week group. The shared control is recorded unsplit exactly as reported; splitting it between duration comparisons is a downstream synthesis step.

interaction_type: Testosterone pretreatment followed by IVF controlled ovarian stimulation
Participant type: Infertile women with poor ovarian response undergoing IVF
Recruitment source: National Center for Reproductive Medicine, Hanoi, Vietnam
